decisions.reason: The confirmed 5V LED supply removes the existing version-dependent condition from the LED board's supply rule.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Doesn't the 5V_EN pin solve this? We can cut the entire 5V rail via GPIO3 when LEDs are not needed, dropping standby current to zero.

decisions.reason: The same source message already introduces the candidate's cutoff behavior, GPIO control, and zero-standby target; the supply-voltage change requires no additional candidate-state modification.
Changing the addressable LED supply to 5V does not alter the listed I2C sensor modules or their 3.3V supply.
The LED supply decision does not change the standalone USB-powered 3.3V rail, its regulator, activation condition, or powered load.
A same-message MODIFY already records the addressable LEDs as loads of the GPIO3-controlled 5V rail and its shutdown behavior, so no additional or corrected Event is required.
Using the existing 5V_EN signal does not change the connector type, pinout, or matching-board interface requirements.
The LED rail decision does not alter the AXP2101 battery, USB, VMID/VSYS, or DCDC1 power-path requirements.
The addressable LED supply change has no effect on battery-connector placement, orientation, spacing, or mounting-hole clearance.
The source decision concerns LED power routing and does not change any component availability, cost, or sourcing policy.
The 5V LED supply decision does not change board dimensions, mounting, enclosure fit, or USB-C placement.
The LED supply and cutoff decision does not resolve or change the battery connector's electrical pinout or physical interface.
The source message does not change BOM completeness, part-number requirements, or the recorded R6 specification.
